The Cook Partisan Voting Index (PVI) is a measure of the competitiveness of a political district, based on the methodology introduced by Rob Richie of the Center for Voting and Democracy (now FairVote) in the Center's July 1997 Monopoly Politics report. The Cook PVI is updated every two years by The Cook Political Report. In 2021, the newsletter ended its relationship with Polidata and instead used Dave Leip's Atlas of U.S. Presidential Elections to calculate the 2020 results. The most recent iteration is the 2022 Cook PVI, which was released with an updated formula for calculating PVI values.

The index looks at how every congressional district voted in the past two presidential elections combined and compares it to the national average. The Cook PVI is displayed as a letter, a plus sign, and a number, with the letter (either a D for Democratic or an R for Republican) indicating the party that won the district and the number showing how many percentage points above the national average it received. In 2022, the formula was updated to weigh the most recent presidential election more heavily.
